subject.title: Feature Request: Enforce skill execution sandbox when enabled: false

question: Should `skills.entries.<key>.enabled:false` become a hard read/exec access boundary for that skill, or should hard isolation use a separate strict policy while `enabled:false` remains an eligibility toggle?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but either direction changes public disabled-skill semantics and crosses filesystem, exec, sandbox, UI/status, docs, and upgrade expectations.

options.title: Make disabled skills hard-denied
options.body: Treat prompt-only hiding as `disable-model-invocation` and centrally deny disabled skill roots for read, write/edit/apply_patch where relevant, exec, sandbox materialization, UI/status, and docs.

options.title: Add separate strict isolation policy
options.body: Keep `enabled:false` as an eligibility toggle for compatibility and add an explicit operator-controlled policy for disabled-skill file and exec denial.

options.title: Document current semantics only
options.body: Clarify that disabled skills are hidden from selection/prompt surfaces only and direct multi-user deployments to sandboxing, tool deny lists, OS users, or containers for enforcement.

recommendation.title: Make disabled skills hard-denied
recommendation.body: Treat prompt-only hiding as `disable-model-invocation` and centrally deny disabled skill roots for read, write/edit/apply_patch where relevant, exec, sandbox materialization, UI/status, and docs.

likelyOwner.reason: This is primarily a security/product boundary choice, and the history links this person to skills documentation and security-direction work around skill trust surfaces.
